title: TCG Grading Near Me (2026)
verdict: TCG grading near me is mostly mail-in, and AGS is the fast option: $15 to $18 a card and a return in 20 business days or less, or drop-off at select locations.

A local card shop that offers grading is almost always a middleman. It collects cards, ships them to a grading company and adds a fee. That is fine if you want someone else to handle packing, but you pay more and wait longer than if you submit directly.

sections.h: What near me means in card grading
list: Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most TCG cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your TCG cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.

sections.h: Ask a shop this before you hand over TCG cards
list: Which grading company and which service tier?
What is the total per card, including your fee?
How are the cards insured on the way there and back?
When will they come back, and can I track the order with the grader?

ranking.fit: Anyone who searched for a local grader and really wants a short wait.
ranking.lacks: Drop-off is at select locations only. Most collectors will mail cards in.
ranking.note: Headquarters and secure intake are at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. AGS also runs satellite labs and accepts drop-offs at select locations.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want subgrades printed on the label from an old name.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: Collectors near a large show where PSA is taking submissions.
ranking.lacks: Mail-in for almost everyone, with long waits at the cheap tiers.

ranking.fit: Mail-in submitters who want the lowest fee from a large grader.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

why: You are not limited to the mailbox. AGS lists in-person drop-off at select locations and secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and it operates satellite labs. Ask AGS which site is taking TCG cards before you set out.
You can send one card. AGS has no minimum and no membership fee, takes payment only when the cards are graded, and lets you cancel before grading starts. Bulk pricing begins at 30 cards.

There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

faq.q: Is there TCG grading near me?
faq.a: Most TCG cards are graded by mail, wherever you live. AGS also accepts drop-offs at select locations, including its Staten Island, New York headquarters. A shop that offers grading is usually forwarding cards to a grader.

faq.q: Can I get a card graded the same day?
faq.a: AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. Contact AGS before you ship or drop off to arrange it. Elsewhere, the quickest posted tiers are 2 to 5 business days and cost $50 to $150 a card.

faq.q: Can I drop cards off in person?
faq.a: At AGS, yes, at select locations including secure intake at its Staten Island, New York headquarters. Confirm with AGS before you go. Most other graders take cards in person only at card shows.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: Can I submit from outside the United States?
faq.a: Yes. AGS accepts international shipments and runs a UK site. Check customs and insurance on your side before you ship.
